questions.q: Once versioning is enabled on a bucket, what actually happens when you run a plain delete on an object?
options: S3 adds a delete marker on top of the existing versions — the object appears gone but the prior versions still exist
The object and all of its prior versions are permanently erased immediately
Versioning blocks all delete operations outright
The delete silently fails with no error and no effect
questions.explain: A plain delete on a versioned object adds a delete marker rather than destroying data — you can remove the marker or restore a specific version ID to recover it.

questions.q: What does a lifecycle rule do on an S3 bucket?
options: Automatically transitions objects to a different storage class or expires them, based purely on their age
Automatically enables versioning on every new object
Grants public read access to objects older than a set number of days
Encrypts objects after a fixed number of days
questions.explain: A lifecycle rule is a bucket (or prefix-scoped) policy that transitions or expires objects automatically by age, instead of requiring someone to move data manually.

questions.q: What's the difference between a bucket policy and an IAM policy for controlling S3 access?
options: A bucket policy is resource-based and attached to the bucket itself, while an IAM policy is identity-based and attached to a user or role
They are two names for the exact same mechanism with no functional difference
A bucket policy only applies to objects smaller than 5GB
An IAM policy can only be used to grant public access, never to restrict it
questions.explain: Bucket policies travel with the bucket and state which principals can do what; IAM policies are attached to a specific user or role and state what that principal can do.

questions.q: What does S3 Block Public Access do?
options: Overrides any bucket policy or ACL that would otherwise make a bucket or its objects publicly accessible
Permanently deletes any object that has ever been made public
Automatically enables versioning on a bucket to protect against public exposure
Blocks all access to a bucket, including from the bucket owner
questions.explain: S3 Block Public Access exists specifically to stop one of the most common real-world cloud data leaks — an accidentally broad policy or legacy ACL granting public access — by overriding it.

questions.q: Why would a lifecycle rule be written to also target noncurrent versions on a versioned bucket?
options: Because old, non-current versions otherwise pile up and keep costing money indefinitely once versioning is turned on
Because noncurrent versions are automatically deleted by AWS after 24 hours regardless of any rule
Because versioning cannot be combined with lifecycle rules at all
Because only noncurrent versions are eligible for the Glacier storage class
questions.explain: Lifecycle rules commonly target noncurrent versions specifically so old versions get transitioned or expired instead of accumulating cost forever.
